central_question: Why do elevator doors start opening before the car actually reaches the floor?
hook: Ever stepped into an elevator and felt the doors begin to slide open a heartbeat before the car even touches the landing? It’s not a glitch—there’s a clever prediction at play.
aha_moment: Elevators predict the car will be almost level and moving slowly enough that the doors can safely start moving in advance, shaving off time while keeping passengers safe.

story_arc.reveal: Doors begin to move before the car arrives

story_arc.purpose: Opening promise: hint at a hidden system
story_arc.reveal: A sensor on the landing tells the controller the car is close enough to start the doors
required_facts: Controller can act on sensor data

story_arc.reveal: Early opening reduces total travel time and smooths the final stop
Infrared/optical strip detects the car’s proximity within ~20 mm
Controller also measures car velocity; only if below ~0.1 m/s does it allow door motion

story_arc.purpose: Midpoint reversal: the car still stops
story_arc.reveal: Even though doors start moving, the car’s brake holds it in place until fully level
Once doors open, the hoist motor is disabled, preventing any movement with doors open
Advance opening cuts stop time by a few seconds, especially in high‑rise buildings

ending_payoff: So the next time you feel those doors creep open early, remember: the elevator’s brain is already predicting your arrival, making the whole ride faster and safer—an invisible choreography you just didn’t see coming.
